newsitem.title: USA: GM's new minivans to start at $20,495.
newsitem.headline: GM's new minivans to start at $20,495.

text.p: General Motors Corp. announced prices Thursday for its new trio of minivans ranging from $20,495 for the base Chevrolet Venture to $26,805 for the top-of-the-line Oldsmobile Silhouette.
The much-anticipated vehicles replace GM's slow-selling, plastic-bodied APV minivans and are beginning to trickle into dealerships.

The Chevrolet Venture will come in four models: a three-door regular wheelbase model starting at $20,495; a three-door extended wheelbase model starting at $21,660; a four-door regular wheelbase model starting at $22,104; and a four-door extended wheelbase model starting at $23,269.
Chevrolet said it expects its volume leader to be the Venture extended wheelbase LS four-door model, which will be popularly equipped at a price of $24,319.
The Pontiac Trans Sport, which is aimed at buyers who want a more sporty vehicle, starts at $21,049 for the regular wheelbase three-door model.
The extended wheelbase three-door Trans Sport starts at $22,009, while the extended wheelbase four-door model starts at $23,939.
Pontiac also is offering "value priced" models equipped with popular options at prices of $23,325 for the regular wheelbase three-door model and $26,125 for the extended wheelbase four-door van.

GM is positioning Oldsmobile's Silhouette as the luxury version of the minivans, with six models ranging in price from $22,245 for the regular wheelbase three-door model to $26,805 for the GLS extended wheelbase four-door model.
Prices for each of the new GM minivans includes a $570 destination charge.
